cards.power: Aliens are real. HIV was a test, and the Illuminati run the DMV. Everything is a dot waiting to be connected.
cards.lore: DISCLOSURE EVENT: Force another player to reveal their hidden agenda (or hand). If they refuse, the aliens take their turn.
cards.gradeReason: You already know this character. They live in your neighbor's garage. Table-ready.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Conspiracy corkboard. Subject: Owl detective connecting dots under UFO. Mood: Paranoid revelation.

cards.power: A timeline of how a secret high council of 'Luciferian' elites supposedly rented out world history.
cards.lore: SHADOW COUNCIL: You may change the Quest Die result by +1/-1 by claiming 'we paid for this outcome.'
cards.gradeReason: SHADOW COUNCIL forces someone to confess the conspiracy. Brutal. Instant kayfabe.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Gothic cartoon. Subject: Octopus in top hat controlling puppet world map. Mood: Ominous conspiracy.

cards.power: From Rome to the Fed: a thesis that usury is the chain and debt is the cage. Lincoln knew too much.
cards.lore: INFLATION: Add a card to the Ring that does nothing but increase the 'cost' (difficulty) for everyone else.
cards.gradeReason: Rome-to-Fed thesis is solid but needs a villain to embody. Descriptive, not quite performative.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Vintage editorial. Subject: Eagle clutching chains made of gold coins over Capitol dome. Mood: Sinister control.

cards.power: 200,000 years of Germanic culture, supposedly stolen and sunk. Jesus was Aryan? Everyone that in the pot too.
cards.lore: MYTHIC REWRITE: Rename an existing location in the Ring to 'Atlantis.' It is now considered 'Lost' and cannot be targeted.
cards.gradeReason: Font artifact garbled the power text. Mythic premise works; execution is half-eaten by the renderer.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Ancient map illumination. Subject: Viking ship sinking toward sunken city glowing below waves. Mood: Lost civilizations.

cards.power: The statistical argument that IQ is destiny, genetics are unfair, and social policy is fighting biology.
cards.lore: STANDARDIZED TEST: Pick a number (1-6). Players who roll under it are 'statistically disadvantaged' and lose their Power this turn.
cards.gradeReason: Statistically disadvantaged mechanic is devastating. Players will feel it in their bones immediately.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Dry academic satire. Subject: Ape and sloth arguing over bell curve graph on chalkboard. Mood: Uncomfortable science.

cards.power: Rosenberg's racial worldview: The soul is race, the blood is truth, and history is a breeding program gone wrong.
cards.lore: PURIST FILTER: Remove any card from the Ring that contradicts your Actor's 'lineage' or 'vibe.'
cards.gradeReason: Rosenberg's worldview in six words. PURIST FILTER removes wrong-lineage cards. Horrifying clarity.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Propaganda poster parody. Subject: Poodle with mirror preaching racial purity to empty chairs. Mood: Ideological horror.

cards.power: A dystopian panic attack about mass migration, the 'Armada,' and the collapse of the West under the weight of the 'Other.'
cards.lore: SIEGE MENTALITY: No new cards may enter the Ring for one full round. The borders are closed.
cards.gradeReason: SIEGE MENTALITY shuts the Ring's borders. The book becomes the mechanic becomes the performance.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Dystopian editorial cartoon. Subject: Frog behind fortress wall watching flood of figures approach. Mood: Paranoid siege.

cards.power: Solzhenitsyn's dense examination of Russian-Jewish relations. Is it history or an indictment? Depends on the translation.
cards.lore: DUAL NARRATIVE: Split the current Reality Ring. Half the players follow one rule, half follow another.
cards.gradeReason: DUAL NARRATIVE split is smart. Solzhenitsyn deserves more than 'depends on translation' to spark performance.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Soviet-era book illustration. Subject: Eagle and bear reading same book from opposite ends. Mood: Contested history.

cards.power: SPECIAL ELITE: Esther Vilar's claim that men are not oppressors, but conditioned slaves working for praise. Feminism is Just HR.
cards.lore: EMOTIONAL BLACKMAIL: Force another player to agree with your narrative or lose their turn.
cards.gradeReason: 'Feminism Is Just HR' landed. EMOTIONAL BLACKMAIL is the whole card — needs the Special Elite frame to click.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Retro satire illustration. Subject: Horse pulling cart, whip held by invisible hand in formal glove. Mood: Conditioned compliance.

cards.power: Class barriers dissolved by four-letter words and an affair in the woods. Banned for obscenity, remembered for honesty.
cards.lore: SCANDAL: Choose two Actor cards. They are now 'entangled'—what happens to one happens to the other.
cards.gradeReason: SCANDAL entangles two players forever. Class, desire, consequences — three words do the work.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Edwardian scandal sheet. Subject: Fox and badger in woodland affair, manor house visible through trees. Mood: Forbidden transgression.

cards.power: A voluntary descent into total objectification. The secret society requires everything. Consent is the first thing to go.
cards.lore: TOTAL SUBMISSION: You may sacrifice your turn to let another player take two turns. Why? Because you enjoy it.
cards.gradeReason: TOTAL SUBMISSION has you sacrificing your turn because you enjoy it. Consent is the mechanic.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Noir graphic novel. Subject: Silhouette descending staircase into candlelit secret society chamber. Mood: Consensual abyss.

cards.power: Weakness is a sin. Pity is a disease. The only right is the iron fist. A manifesto for social Darwinists.
cards.lore: ALPHA STRIKE: Overwrite any card in the Ring immediately. No narrative justification needed. Might makes right.
cards.gradeReason: ALPHA STRIKE needs no justification. Overwrite. Dominate. The card IS the manifesto.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Social Darwinist propaganda parody. Subject: Honey badger on skull throne crushing books with iron fist. Mood: Brutal dominance.

cards.power: Witchcraft! Occultism! This boy wizard is a gateway drug to Satanism, according to Tennessee exorcists.
cards.lore: EXPELLIARMUS: Disarm another player. They cannot use their Artifact's Power this turn.
cards.gradeReason: EXPELLIARMUS from a witchcraft-banned book is pure satirical kayfabe — G2 for outsiders, G1 for fandom.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Banned-book irony poster. Subject: Rabbit wizard casting spell at horrified church elders. Mood: Comical moral panic.

cards.power: The most printed book in history, yet banned in 50+ countries. Dangerous in authoritarian states, mandatory in others.
cards.lore: DIVINE INTERVENTION: Reroll the Quest Die. If it's a 1, a plague hits [clear the Ring].
cards.gradeReason: Banned in 50 countries, mandatory in others. DIVINE INTERVENTION rerolls and may plague everyone. Perfect framing.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Split-panel diptych. Subject: Same Bible burning in one panel, stamped mandatory in another. Mood: Sacred and forbidden.

cards.power: Holden Caulfield's nervous breakdown. Banned for swearing and rebellion. Everyone is a phony except you.
cards.lore: ALIENATION: You are immune to all effects from other players this turn. You're just wandering New York alone.
cards.gradeReason: ALIENATION makes you immune this turn. You're just wandering New York alone. Perfect.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: 1950s New York illustration. Subject: Duck in red hunting cap wandering Manhattan ignoring everyone. Mood: Alienated adolescence.

cards.power: A book about burning books that gets burned for being about burning books. The irony burns at 451 degrees.
cards.lore: MEMORY HOLE: Burn (remove) one card from the game permanently. It is never mentioned again.
cards.gradeReason: A book about burning books gets burned. MEMORY HOLE erases a card forever. G1 perfection.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Self-consuming irony poster. Subject: Firefly burning stack of books, top book labeled Fahrenheit 451. Mood: Recursive prohibition.

cards.power: Consumerism meets carnage. Patrick Bateman murders his way through the 80s, but the real horror is that nobody notices.
cards.lore: RETURNING VIDEO TAPES: Leave the scene (skip your turn) to avoid consequences. When you return, the Ring is clean.
cards.gradeReason: RETURNING VIDEO TAPES skips your turn because Bateman needs an alibi. Genius mechanic naming.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: 80s corporate noir. Subject: Wolf in suit rewinding VHS tape, bloody axe hidden behind back. Mood: Carnage as normalcy.

cards.power: The gun culture bible. A fiction so detailed about dismantling the ATF that it became a manual for McVeigh.
cards.lore: REPEAL: Nullify the current Quest. The laws have changed because you have more ammo.
cards.gradeReason: McVeigh reference is striking. REPEAL is clean. G2 — obscure book needs introduction before performance clicks.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Militia manual cover parody. Subject: Armadillo in tactical gear dismantling government building with blueprints. Mood: Armed resistance.

cards.cardName: All Quiet on the Western Front
cards.power: War is not heroic; it is a meat grinder. Banned by Nazis for being 'unpatriotic' because it showed the trauma, not the glory.
cards.lore: SHELL SHOCK: All players must remain silent for one minute. No narration. Only the dice move.
cards.gradeReason: SHELL SHOCK: total silence, one minute, no narration. Best single mechanic in the deck.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: WW1 trench realism. Subject: Butterfly landing on muddy soldier's outstretched hand in silent trench. Mood: Brutal silence.

cards.power: The Sun of Knowledge. An ancient grimoire of names and numbers. Sufi wisdom or black magic? Don't read it.
cards.lore: DJINN SUMMONING: Roll a D6. On a 6, you win the current conflict instantly. On a 1, you lose your Actor card.
cards.gradeReason: High-stakes DJINN SUMMONING is compelling. Obscure enough to need a brief at table before performance lands.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Islamic manuscript illumination parody. Subject: Black cat summoning djinn from glowing Arabic text grimoire. Mood: Ancient forbidden power.

verdict: Uncle FrizzleBob just got CONTRA-BANNED from his own manifesto. This deck is the most compact punch in the corpus — 20 cards, zero filler, every title doing its job from across the room. The mechanic-to-meaning ratio is best-in-class: Shell Shock silences the whole table, Memory Hole erases a card forever, Returning Video Tapes skips your turn because you need an alibi. One miss: 'Atlantis, Edda, and Bible' has garbled power text — font artifact ate the sentence mid-thought. Twenty books, twenty weapons. Table-ready: YES.
blurb: Banned classics, conspiracy bibles, and literary contraband in one 20-card deck. For anyone who thinks the most dangerous thing in a room is a book.

marketingText:
Kayfabizarro: THE MOST SUPPRESSED BOOKS – Banned Classics, Conspiracy Bibles & Literary Contraband (Free Cut & Play Comic Card Game)

The most dangerous object in any room is still a book somebody told you not to open.

Every suppressed book arrives with a helpful label, attached by someone who read it so you would not have to. Too violent. Too obscene. Too true. Too stupid. The label is the actual product. Whoever controls the warning sticker decides which thoughts reach you already chewed, and they would love for you to mistake their fear for your protection. This deck peels the stickers off and leaves them off.

Twenty cut-and-play cards turn the forbidden shelf into a fighting roster. This is Social Story Wrestling: you drag a book into the ring, perform its case out loud with a straight face, and the table rules whether it earns its banned reputation or folds the moment anyone actually opens it.

WHAT'S INSIDE?
- The Forbidden Shelf Core Deck: 20 High-Res "Print, Cut & Play" Cards, featuring All Quiet on the Western Front, Fahrenheit 451, and American Psycho, racked without comment beside Behold a Pale Horse, Might is Right, and The Bible.
- The Freestyle Rules: The complete Anti-Rulebook, one page of it titled "How to Weaponize This Paper." No complicated math, just storytelling, dice-driven chaos, and a roster that will never tell you which titles are genius and which are poison.
- The Manifesto Back-Page: the deck's own confession that some of these books are evil, some are brilliant, some are just boring, and the sorting is your job now. Cut them out. Play them. Don't believe them.

WHY "PAY WHAT YOU WANT"?
A free shelf is the only shelf nobody can quietly curate. Are you broke? Enter "0" and take the whole contraband stack. Read it. Play it. Argue with it. Want to support the craft? Every dollar goes straight into the next deck of things someone would rather you never shuffled.

Choose your reality. Become an Epistemic Outlaw.
They never bother to ban the books that change nothing.
Stay fluffy. — Uncle FrizzleBob
